reason: The text illustrates this principle through Eli's negative example. God explicitly judges Eli's household because Eli knew his sons were doing wrong but failed to restrain them (וְלֹא כִהָה בָּם - 'he did not restrain them'). God pronounces judgment 'because of the iniquity which he knew' - establishing that a leader bears accountability for the actions of those under their authority when they fail to exercise proper oversight. Eli's failure to take responsibility for correcting his sons' wrongdoing and his indirect responsibility for the people's spiritual welfare resulted in direct judgment on his house. The text demonstrates that leadership inherently carries the burden of accountability for both the leader's actions and the actions of those they oversee.
